subject: Clarify: customer output consent / feedback license for Novum Order Form
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@novumanalytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novum Procurement <procurement@novumanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form questions re: output ownership and training

Markus —

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement and legal have a few open items in the draft MSA/Order Form we exchanged last week. Can you confirm Redwood's position on two points so we can proceed: 

1) Output ownership: does Novum own outputs generated when our users submit prompts derived from Novum data? We want explicit customer ownership of outputs that are derived from customer-provided input.

2) Training / model improvements: does Redwood intend to use Novum data or Novum-generated outputs to train models or improve the service? If so, what form of license are you seeking? We need clarifying language for the Order Form (Exhibit A) and for procurement to sign off.

Procurement would also like an evidence list (audit log or sample telemetry) that shows how customer inputs are isolated and what falls under feedback telemetry. I've attached the MSA with our redline (Novum_MSA_Redline_v1.pdf).

Can you send suggested contract language and the evidence checklist by EOD Monday? We're targeting signature next week.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Senior Counsel, Novum Analytics

Attachment: Novum_MSA_Redline_v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@novumanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form questions re: output ownership and training

Susan —

Appreciate the clear ask. High level answers up front and then proposed language below. We can iterate whatever your counsel prefers.

High level:
- Outputs: Novum retains ownership of Customer Data and any outputs that are the "direct result" of Customer Data (we suggest the phrase below to limit ambiguity). Redwood requests the right to serve, cache, and transmit outputs for delivery and diagnostics only.
- Training: Redwood will not retrain or add to model weights using identifiable Novum Customer Data or Customer Content unless Novum opts in via the Order Form. However, we do collect minimal, aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized token usage) for service quality. For product improvement, we request a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback license covering de-identified service feedback unless Novum opts out.

Proposed contract snippets (for your redline):

1) Output ownership (Order Form / Exhibit A)
"Customer Content" means content, data and prompts that Customer or its End Users supply to the Service. Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and in any Outputs that are the direct and intended result of Customer Content. "Outputs" do not include model-level improvements, aggregated metrics, or de-identified feedback described in Section 3.

2) Training and feedback license (MSA – new clause)
"Feedback License": Customer grants to Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual license to use de-identified, aggregated behavioral data and system telemetry ("Feedback") solely to operate, improve and secure the Service, subject to Customer's right to opt out in the Order Form. Feedback shall not include Customer Content or Outputs that are reasonably identifiable as derived from Customer Content without Customer's prior written consent.

I'll attach a short evidence checklist that Procurement can use. See attached: evidence_request_checklist.pdf.

Next steps: Laura + Monica, can you review and add any operational constraints (telemetry retention, access controls) we should include? Susan, if Novum legal prefers narrower language on the feedback license, propose edits and we will respond quickly.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_request_checklist.pdf; Novum_MSA_Redline_v1.pdf (from you)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Susan Park <susan.park@novumanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form questions re: output ownership and training

Markus / Susan —

Couple operational points to add so procurement can see how this will be implemented: 

- Telemetry scope: propose a short exhibit that enumerates fields we collect as Feedback (e.g., request_id, request latency, model variant id, token counts, error codes) and expressly exclude prompt text and generated content.
- Retention: feedback telemetry retained 90 days by default (we can offer 30/90/365 in Dedicated/Enterprise). Put that in Exhibit B.
- Access controls: only CS/Trust engineers will get access to raw telemetry, and access will be logged; provide SOC2-reportable controls language.

Draft language for Exhibit B (Operational Controls):
- Telemetry fields: request_id, timestamp, model_id, response_status, token_count, latency_ms.
- Redaction: prompt text and full outputs are redacted prior to inclusion in feedback aggregates.
- Access: restricted to authorized Redwood personnel; access requests for customer-specific troubleshooting will be logged and can be audited.

If Novum wants stricter retention or a dedicated log-forwarding arrangement, we can include optional order form items and pricing.

Laura
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Park <susan.park@novumanalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novum Procurement <procurement@novumanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form questions re: output ownership and training

Thanks Laura — this is helpful. A few follow-ups after internal review: 

1) The phrase "direct and intended result" is a bit vague. Our engineering team asked whether derivative outputs that rephrase or summarize Customer Content could fall outside "Outputs" under that definition. Can Redwood propose an objective test (e.g., based on string overlap or prompt lineage) or confirm that derivative summaries will be treated as Customer Outputs if they materially rely on Customer Content.

2) Feedback license: Novum is open to a limited feedback license for de-identified telemetry, but we need a commitment that any data used for model training will never include customer-specific prompts or outputs unless Novum opts in on the Order Form. Please confirm the technical safeguards Redwood uses to segregate Customer Content from training corpora.

3) Evidence requested: procurement would like a one-page technical memo showing: (a) where data is stored, (b) how KV cache/prefix caching is isolated per customer, (c) how we prevent cross-customer contamination during batching, and (d) sample logs (sanitized) that show token-level redaction. Can Redwood provide that memo and sample logs for procurement review? See attached spreadsheet for line-item questions (redline_comments_novum.xlsx).

If you can produce the memo + proposed redline language by Tuesday EOD, we can keep the signature cadence.

Regards,
Susan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@novumanalytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form questions re: output ownership and training

Susan —

Quick reply on the technical guarantees and a suggested narrow clause for training: 

Technical safeguards (summary):
- Customer data stored in tenant-isolated buckets with per-tenant KMS keys; no plaintext replication across tenants.
- Serving layer: per-request routing uses tenant token to ensure KV caches and prefix caches are partitioned. No request is batched across tenants unless explicitly configured by the customer (not default).
- Training corpora: our model training pipeline ingests only opt-in datasets. Engineering maintains a curated pipeline; no live production customer content flows into training without manual review and a signed opt-in.

Suggested training clause (add to MSA):
"Training Exclusion": Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs to train, fine-tune, or update production model weights except where Customer has provided explicit, written opt-in on the Order Form. For avoidance of doubt, Logs and de-identified operational metrics necessary to maintain service quality are excluded from this restriction provided they are processed as described in Exhibit B.

We'll prepare the one-page technical memo and sanitized sample logs for your review by EOD Tuesday.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
